name: publicWeb_getDirectMessageRequests
description: Web member's door to HC6.hcapp_getDirectMessageRequests (E9.F1.S19): pending requests from other hashers to message the member, shown with Accept / Decline. Read-only. A thin wrapper that EXECs the app SP and returns its rowsets unchanged. Auth: the wrapped SP's HC6.ValidateAppAuth — token signed for hcapp_getDirectMessageRequests; scoped to the token's user.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The browser's HC.Device id (the web member session). No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token signed for hcapp_getDirectMessageRequests (the SP that validates it). No SQL default.

rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_getDirectMessageRequests: Auth failure (ValidateAppAuth) returns the error detail alone and the SP returns. No compact envelope.

rowsets.name: Requests
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_getDirectMessageRequests: On success: one row per pending request, newest first (ORDER BY HasherFriendMap.createdAt DESC). Empty when nothing is pending.

columns.name: FromPublicHasherId
columns.description: UPPER(CAST(Hasher.PublicHasherId AS NVARCHAR(40))) of the requester; the app lowercases it on arrival.

columns.name: RequestedAt
columns.description: HasherFriendMap.createdAt of the requester's row — when they asked (column added by db/hc6/app/archive/2026-09-29_hasher_block.sql).

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.hcapp_getDirectMessageRequests with the same arguments — every side effect is the wrapped SP's:
None on success. INSERT HC.ErrorLog then THROW on an unhandled error (CATCH, line 50).
INSERT HC.ErrorLog ('<web>', userId NULL, deviceId) then THROW in the wrapper's CATCH, for an error the wrapped SP does not handle itself.

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId and @accessToken have no SQL default (line 15). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.
The wrapped SP's CATCH logs to HC.ErrorLog and THROWs; this wrapper's CATCH (lines 24-29) catches the re-raise and logs a second row for the same failure.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
